items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: She said that Buddy Bowman, that's the only thing I knew about it.

ctx.x: Did you ever hear Buddy Bowman the first time?

Well, I tell you, I heard him, but I didn't see him and my mama told me we was living in the back of Police of Burns Hall. We lived on the airport street and Police of Burns Hall happened to be on Village Street and we lived in the back of Police of Burns Hall and every Monday used to have a lot of banquets. We called them banquets. People nowadays say banquets. I said banquets. Every Monday had a banquets at this particular hall, nearly every Monday. And especially Monday, well, my mama told me that Buddy Bowman…

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: My mom happened to call to say, that's Buddy Bowling blowing over there. That man sure can blow.

ctx.x: Where? What part of this city?

I was born at New Orleans, Louisiana, at Barracks and St. Claude, right on the corner of Barracks and St. Claude. I did remember hearing Buddy Bowling because Buddy Bowling was playing a banquet at the place of Burns Hall. That's on Burrow between Annette and Seminole. And I was living on Equat in the back back back street from the Hall between Annette and Seminole. And Buddy was Buddy Bowling. The band was blowing. And the people was dancing, I imagine. And having a good time. My mom happened to call to say,…
